messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] PagerDuty: P1002 - CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED on gpu-pool-east-2-3
incident-bot: severity: P0
incident-bot: affected: serving/runtime/gpu-pool-east-2
incident-bot: symptom: spike in cudaAlloc failures, autoshedder firing, ~12 nodes showing OOMs
alex: Just got the page, looking
alex: metrics look like rapid vmem growth, KV cache evictions also up: https://internal.grafana/redwood/gpu-alloc
maya: I'm on it, starting with pool health check
sam: pinging pagerduty to see if it's acknowledged
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert P1002 acknowledged by alex (oncall)
alex: acked, adding context: customer impact on Dedicated customers in us-east, some requests 500ing
alex: running: kubectl get pods -n runtime -l pool=gpu-east-2 -o wide
alex: output:
```
node/gpu-pool-east-2-3   Ready   1/1   400m   192.168.10.35   <none>
pod/runner-abc123        CrashLoopBackOff 1/1  2m
pod/runner-def456        Running  1/1   10m
```
maya: seeing NVidia driver logs showing repeated cudaMalloc retries and 'out of memory' traces; suspects KV cache plus long-tail inference requests causing fragmentation
devops-sarah: can we temporarily scale down eviction thresholds / force-evac? what's the plan for immediate mitigation
sam: suggest 1) drain the worst nodes 2) enable model fallback to smaller quantized variant 3) enable aggressive kvcache eviction
alex: starting node drain on gpu-pool-east-2-3: `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-east-2-3 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-pool-east-2-3`
maya: triggering model fallback via routing: `redwoodctl route update --pool gpu-east-2 --fallback smaller-quant-v1 --immediate`
sam: applying kvcache policy change: `POST /internal/config/batching` body: `{ "kv_cache_max_entries": 200000 }` — temporary until rollback
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to level 2 (no response from second oncall)
maya: customers impacted: 5 Dedicated tenants in us-east, degraded throughput, errors ~15% on gen endpoints
alex: opened incident ticket INC-2024-513, triage notes in ticket
sam: monitoring for drop in cudaAlloc errors
incident-bot: Auto-shedder logs: 2024-06-01T12:02:40Z - prefault fail - retval=-12
maya: after drain + fallback, observed down from 80 cudaAlloc failures/min to 3/min in 4m
devops-sarah: rolling restart on remaining at-risk nodes to defragment GPU memory: `systemctl restart nvidia-docker` scheduled
alex: next: escalate to infra if persistent; for now continue monitoring; handoff in 30m to night oncall
maya: note for handoff: WIP mitigations, rollback commands:
```
redwoodctl route update --pool gpu-east-2 --fallback none
kubectl uncordon gpu-pool-east-2-3
POST /internal/config/batching { \"kv_cache_max_entries\": 500000 }
```
sam: adding timeline to incident ticket
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert resolved (closed) by alex
alex: closing this thread, will follow up in postmortem; if anything reoccurs ping me
